questions.question: How far before a school bus stop should the flashing lights turn on?

options.text: At least 50 feet
At least 100 feet
At least 200 feet
At least 1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 200 feet
questions.explanation: School bus flashing amber lights should turn on at least 200 feet before the bus stops.

questions.question: When is an outside convex mirror properly adjusted?

options.text: The driver can see at least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
The driver can see the front bumper.
The driver can see the top of the bus.
The driver can see the front windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see at least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The side mirrors should show at least one traffic lane on each side of the bus and the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts. The driver should also see where the rear tires touch the ground.

questions.question: Where are outside convex mirrors located on a bus?

options.text: Below the outside flat mirrors.
Above the outside flat mirrors.
Next to the door.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Below the outside flat mirrors.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are placed below the flat mirrors. They help the driver see a wider view of traffic, clearance, and students around the bus.

questions.question: Before backing into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Pull directly into the alley parking space.
Turn your vehicle to the right to position yourself directly in front of the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer boundary.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: First, pull past the alley and stop your vehicle parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner has instructed it to be.
Within five feet of the final position described by the examiner.
Wherever you can safely park.
Within two feet of the final position described by the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner has instructed it to be.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be in the exact position the examiner described. Not following this instruction exactly can result in failing the test.

questions.question: What counts as a "look" during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Walking to the back of a vehicle to check its position
Using side mirrors to check a vehicle's position
Looking out of the driver's side window to check a vehicle's position
A driver glancing over their shoulder to check blind spots

questions.correctAnswerText: Walking to the back of a vehicle to check its position
questions.explanation: A "look" is when you open the door, leave your seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check where it is. On the straight line backing exercise, you can only do this once. On other exercises, you can do this twice.

questions.question: During other exercises, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.
Four times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position twice during any exercise except straight line backing. For straight line backing, you can only do this once.

questions.question: What causes the most student deaths per year?

options.text: Students loading and unloading a school bus
Accidents involving drunk drivers
Accidents involving negligence
Accidents in which drivers ignore traffic signals or signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Students loading and unloading a school bus
questions.explanation: More students are killed getting on or off school buses than while riding inside them.

questions.question: If a student drops an item near a stopped bus, what should they do?

options.text: Hurry and pick up the item.
Leave the item behind.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.
Have another student pick it up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items themselves because they could move out of the driver's sight. Instead, students should get the driver's attention and ask the driver to retrieve the item.

questions.question: What should properly adjusted outside convex mirrors show?

options.text: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
The front of the bus.
The rear door of the bus.
The top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors should show at least one traffic lane on each side, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, after you drive over a bridge, the examiner may ask you to recall something about it.

options.text: The posted weight limit.
The color of a sign you just passed.
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge.
Whether there was a crosswalk on the bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The posted weight limit.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, the examiner may ask you to remember the weight limit sign on a bridge you just drove over.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time
Two times
Three times
Four times

questions.correctAnswerText: One time
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle only one time during the straight line backing exercise to check where it is positioned.

questions.question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus especially dangerous for students?

options.text: The sun reflects off the left side of the bus and makes it hard to see.
Other vehicles are passing on the left side of the bus.
It is hard to see the left side of any bus.
There is no door on the left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other vehicles are passing on the left side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The left side of a school bus is especially dangerous because vehicles pass by on that side.

questions.question: What do outside crossover mirrors let a driver see?

options.text: The front bumper
The rear bumper
The right side of the bus
The left side of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see the front bumper, the danger zone directly in front of the bus, and the areas to the left and right sides from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: When students exit the bus at a school, the driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Leave the key in the ignition and leave the driver's area.
Read a book while students exit.
Not be on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: When dropping off children, turn off the engine. Remove the key if you leave the driver's area.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to perform which maneuver?

options.text: Alley dock.
Parallel park to your right.
Parallel park to your left.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: To complete an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: First pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When alley docking, your vehicle should be parked:

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight and within the parking space boundaries.
At an angle within the parking space boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight and within the parking space boundaries.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle into the alley. Your vehicle must be parked straight and stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Why should a school bus stop a short distance away from waiting students?

options.text: Students will walk to the bus, making it easier for the driver to watch them.
Students usually wait on a sidewalk.
Students may get scared of the bus coming toward them.
Buses are hard to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students will walk to the bus, making it easier for the driver to watch them.
questions.explanation: A school bus should stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students. This way, students must walk toward the bus, and the driver can watch their movements more easily.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and students must exit the bus, where should they go?

options.text: To a nearby building
To the closest tree
Near a river
To a mountain

questions.correctAnswerText: To a nearby building
questions.explanation: If students must exit due to a tornado, the driver should take them to shelter in a nearby building. If no building is available, lead them to a ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that could flood and stay far enough away so a tipping bus won't hit them.
